introduction.zh: 面对一个普通问题，你更想先检视定义、考虑具体合宜，还是重新审视自己的尺度、彼此自由或眼前回应？本版以18道原创四选一提供九个哲学阅读入口：苏格拉底、亚里士多德、孔子、老子、伊壁鸠鲁、爱比克泰德、尼采、波伏瓦和马可·奥勒留。名称只关联所选原典中的有限问题，不替古人答题，不测试你像不像真实人物，也不代表赞同完整学说。全部作答后看相对次数和所有最高并列，九份完整说明也可先读。
introduction.en: When considering an ordinary question, would you first examine meanings, consider appropriate practice, reconsider your standards, attend to freedom with others or reflect on your present response? Eighteen original choices offer nine reading entrances: Socrates, Aristotle, Confucius, Laozi, Epicurus, Epictetus, Nietzsche, Simone de Beauvoir and Marcus Aurelius. Each name associates with limited questions in selected primary texts rather than supplying historical answers, testing personal resemblance or endorsing an entire doctrine. Complete the set for relative counts and every highest tie, or read all nine full guides first.

instructions.zh: 按你目前更想优先考虑的思路完成18道原创四选一，不选哪个哲学家更有名或哪句更高尚。九个阅读联想各出现8次，每个位置2次；每次选择加1，0反向。全部完成才看相对次数与全部最高并列，不硬派主副型或相似度百分比。选项是当代阅读提示，不声称原哲学家会这样答题，也不等于赞同他们的完整思想。新版改变了对象与部分选项，新旧计数不直接互认，也不表示思想、道德、人格或能力的进退。可以直接先读九份全文或退出。
instructions.en: Complete eighteen original choices using the line of inquiry you currently want to consider first rather than the most famous name or noblest-sounding sentence. Nine reading associations each appear eight times and twice in each position. Each choice adds one count with no reverse keys. Complete the set for relative counts and every highest tie without a forced secondary type or similarity percentage. Options are contemporary reading prompts, not historical answers or endorsements of whole systems. This edition changes the figures and some options; old and new counts are not interchangeable or evidence of intellectual, moral, personality or ability progress or decline. You may read all nine full guides first or leave.

prompt.zh: 朋友说某个活动安排“很公平”，你更想先沿哪条思路讨论？
prompt.en: A friend calls an activity arrangement fair. Which line of inquiry would you explore first?

label.zh: 先问公平具体指什么，哪些例子会推翻这个说法
label.en: Ask what fair means and which examples would challenge the claim

label.zh: 看反复照这样行动会养成什么做法，是否适合具体处境
label.en: Consider the practice repeated actions build and whether it fits the circumstances

label.zh: 这种安排是否让每个人仍能选择和提出自己的计划，而不是由一个人替大家决定
label.en: Whether the arrangement leaves each person able to choose and propose a project rather than having one person decide for everyone

label.zh: 看看所求的好处是否值得随之增加的麻烦与欲望
label.en: Consider whether the desired benefit is worth its added trouble and wants

prompt.zh: 一个读书小组想把讨论变得更好，你更愿意提出什么理由？
prompt.en: A reading group wants better discussions. Which reason would you offer?

label.zh: 再多规则也替不了此刻认真回应别人、把眼前这一轮谈话做好
label.en: More rules cannot replace responding considerately to others and attending to the conversation at hand

label.zh: 讨论要让每个人能提出自己的问题，也让这些选择有机会被别人接续
label.en: Discussion should leave people able to pose their own questions and let others carry those possibilities further

label.zh: 也许先少加几条控制发言的规则，看看会怎样
label.en: Perhaps remove some attempts to control contributions and observe what happens

label.zh: 好的讨论也容许我们重估自己维护的标准，而不只加固原有结论
label.en: Good discussion can involve reconsidering the standards we defend rather than only reinforcing existing conclusions

prompt.zh: 有人把礼貌理解成永远附和，你更想怎样回应？
prompt.en: Someone equates courtesy with always agreeing. How would you approach that?

label.zh: 礼与相处需要真诚和反省，不能只剩表面附和
label.en: Courtesy in relationships needs sincerity and reflection rather than surface agreement

label.zh: 看看是否为了维持一种样子而过度安排彼此
label.en: Ask whether maintaining appearances leads to excessive interference

label.zh: 即使不赞同，也可检视自己的判断，用不贬低对方的方式说清眼前的分歧
label.en: Even in disagreement, examine my judgment and explain the present difference without belittling the other person

label.zh: 让对方保留不同看法，也承担自己表达分歧的责任，不把附和当作参与条件
label.en: Leave the other person free to differ while taking responsibility for my disagreement, without making agreement a condition of participation

prompt.zh: 为一个轻松周末定下许多目标后，你更想考虑哪种问题？
prompt.en: After setting many goals for a relaxed weekend, which question interests you?

label.zh: 我的计划是否给同伴留下真实选择，也承认自己要为安排带来的影响负责
label.en: Whether my plan leaves companions a genuine choice while acknowledging responsibility for its effects

label.zh: 哪些愿望是需要，哪些只会继续抬高满足的门槛
label.en: Which desires meet needs and which keep raising the threshold of satisfaction

label.zh: 哪些选择与努力属于自己，哪些结果不能保证
label.en: Which choices and efforts are mine and which outcomes cannot be guaranteed

label.zh: 先把眼前能认真完成的一件事做好，不让对整个周末的想象带走注意
label.en: Attend carefully to one thing available now rather than letting an imagined whole weekend carry my attention away

prompt.zh: 看到一件有趣但并不需要的小物，你更想先思考？
prompt.en: You notice an appealing object you do not need. What would you consider first?

label.zh: 拥有它的乐趣与之后的维护、惦记是否相称
label.en: Whether its enjoyment is worth the upkeep and further wanting

label.zh: 想要与决定如何行动属于我，但别人怎样评价不由我决定
label.en: My desire and chosen action are mine, while others’ evaluations are not

label.zh: 这份想要来自我愿承担的追求，还是沿用了“拥有才算进步”的尺度
label.en: Whether this desire belongs to a pursuit I would choose or repeats an inherited standard that acquiring means progressing

label.zh: 这个选择会怎样影响与共同使用空间的人守约相处
label.en: How the choice affects keeping agreements with people sharing the space

prompt.zh: 一份认真准备的小展示没有得到预期回应，你更想讨论？
prompt.en: A carefully prepared small display gets an unexpected response. What would you examine?

label.zh: 自己的判断和行动与无法保证的回应之间的区别
label.en: The difference between my judgment and actions and a response I cannot guarantee

label.zh: 什么依据让我们认定这次一定不成功
label.en: The grounds for calling it an unsuccessful attempt

label.zh: 哪些具体做法值得继续练习，而非只盯一次结果
label.en: Which particular practices deserve repetition rather than judging only one outcome

label.zh: 我是否承认观众可以另作理解，而不把他们的回应当成作品必须拥有的东西
label.en: Whether I acknowledge the audience’s freedom to interpret rather than treating its response as something my work must possess

prompt.zh: 有人说“只要知识够多，人就会做得好”，你更想问？
prompt.en: Someone says enough knowledge ensures good action. Which response would you explore?

label.zh: 知识若只是加固旧的自我评价，是否还需要重估自己所追求的标准
label.en: Whether knowledge that only reinforces an old self-evaluation leaves the standards I pursue unexamined

label.zh: 知道说法与在具体行动中反复养成合宜做法是否相同
label.en: Whether knowing an account equals developing appropriate practice through repeated action

label.zh: 学与思是否都参与其中，日常相处是否体现所学
label.en: Whether learning and reflection both matter and appear in everyday relationships

label.zh: 更多知识带来的追求是否真让生活更易满足
label.en: Whether the pursuits added by more knowledge make life easier to satisfy

prompt.zh: 社区讨论一个大家遵循已久的小习惯，你更想从哪里看？
prompt.en: A community discusses a long-standing small custom. Where would you begin?

label.zh: 在今天的具体情形里，这个做法是否仍然合宜
label.en: Whether the practice remains appropriate to today’s particulars

label.zh: 它是否在实际相处中保留真诚、尊重和反省
label.en: Whether it supports sincerity, respect and reflection in actual relationships

label.zh: 是否把可自然调整的事情用过多干预固定下来
label.en: Whether too much intervention fixes what could adjust without forcing

label.zh: 我如何判断和选择是一回事，别人是否改变是另一回事
label.en: My judgment and choice are one matter; whether others change is another

prompt.zh: 和朋友约定共同学习，你更重视讨论哪一点？
prompt.en: When agreeing to learn with a friend, which point would you examine?

label.zh: 学习也要落实为彼此守信与愿意反省的相处
label.en: Learning should appear in trustworthy, reflective dealings with one another

label.zh: 少一些强行统一进度，是否反而容得下各自学习
label.en: Whether less forced uniformity in pace leaves more room for learning

label.zh: 计划满足了实际需要，还是不断制造更多要完成的事
label.en: Whether the plan meets needs or keeps creating more things to want completed

label.zh: 我们为何认为相同进度就等于学得好
label.en: Why we assume identical progress means learning well

prompt.zh: 整理一个本来已经能用的空间时，你更想思考？
prompt.en: While rearranging a space that already works, what would you consider?

label.zh: 哪些改动是在强求理想样子，是否可以少做一点
label.en: Which changes force an ideal appearance and whether less intervention would suffice

label.zh: 这次改变是在延续习惯，还是在实践自己重新选择的生活取向
label.en: Whether this change merely continues a habit or expresses a direction of life I have chosen anew

label.zh: 我能选择怎样整理，但无法决定所有人的观感
label.en: I can choose my arrangement without determining everyone’s impressions

label.zh: 针对这里的人与用途，怎样才是合宜而非机械折中
label.en: What fits these people and uses rather than a mechanical compromise

prompt.zh: 有人把享受生活理解成不断增加刺激，你更愿意讨论？
prompt.en: Someone equates enjoying life with continually adding stimulation. What interests you?

label.zh: 每一种快乐是否都值得选择，要看随后带来的影响
label.en: Whether every pleasure is worth choosing given what follows

label.zh: 我们如何面对自己的欲望，与能否得到每个结果并非一回事
label.en: How we approach desires differs from obtaining every outcome

label.zh: 享受这个词是否只有增加刺激这一种解释
label.en: Whether enjoyment has only this interpretation of increasing stimulation

label.zh: 此刻怎样对待人、怎样完成手上的事也值得注意，不必让刺激多少决定这一刻的价值
label.en: How I treat people and attend to the task at hand also matters, without making stimulation determine the moment’s value

prompt.zh: 轻松活动因天气改变计划，你更想沿哪条思路回应？
prompt.en: Weather changes plans for a relaxed activity. Which reasoning appeals first?

label.zh: 改变安排时，相关的人是否仍能选择，而不是因为我投入过就必须跟随
label.en: Whether others retain a choice in the revised arrangement rather than having to follow because I invested in it

label.zh: 天气改变后，此刻仍能清楚说明自己的打算，并以合作的方式回应同伴
label.en: Despite changed weather, I can state my present intention clearly and respond cooperatively to companions

label.zh: 能否不把原计划当成必须证明自己的标准，重新创造这次活动值得做的理由
label.en: Whether I can stop treating the original plan as a test of myself and reconsider what makes the activity worth choosing

label.zh: 少强求原安排，看看现有条件允许什么展开
label.en: Reduce the forcing of the original arrangement and see what conditions allow

prompt.zh: 一个讨论里大家都说“这很显然”，你最想先做？
prompt.en: Everyone in a discussion calls something obvious. What would you examine first?

label.zh: 请大家说清依据，承认哪些部分其实还不知道
label.en: Ask for grounds and acknowledge what remains unknown

label.zh: 谁的选择余地在这个“显然”的结论里被忽略，谁还能提出不同方向
label.en: Whose possibilities are overlooked by this obvious conclusion and who remains able to propose another direction

label.zh: 反省自己是否认真听和学，而不只是跟着附和
label.en: Reflect on whether I listened and learned rather than merely agreed

label.zh: 我是否把继承的评价当成自己的尺度，愿不愿重新承担选择
label.en: Whether I mistake inherited evaluations for my own standards and am willing to choose them anew

prompt.zh: 朋友想用一条规则处理所有小分歧，你更想提醒？
prompt.en: A friend wants one rule for every minor disagreement. What would you raise?

label.zh: 具体人、时间和目的不同，合宜做法不能只是同一个中点
label.en: Different people, times and purposes call for more than an identical midpoint

label.zh: 相处中的真诚和尊重需要反省，不能只靠形式
label.en: Sincerity and respect in relationships require reflection rather than form alone

label.zh: 规则不能替我判断眼前怎样回应，尤其不能把不同意见的人都当成麻烦
label.en: A rule cannot replace judging my present response, especially if it makes everyone who differs seem troublesome

label.zh: 自己的判断可以检视，但他人怎样回应不能完全支配
label.en: I can examine my judgment without fully commanding others’ responses

prompt.zh: 你想理解一项承诺的意义，更愿意从哪一点开始？
prompt.en: To understand a commitment, where would you begin?

label.zh: 此刻能否用公正、清楚的行动履行它，而不把价值放在别人是否称赞
label.en: Whether I can act on it fairly and clearly now without placing its value in others’ praise

label.zh: 这项承诺是在延续旧的自我要求，还是经过检视仍愿承担的取向
label.en: Whether this commitment repeats an old demand on myself or expresses a direction I would still choose after reconsideration

label.zh: 想清追求这项承诺的回报会不会带来更多难满足的欲望
label.en: Consider whether seeking its rewards creates further difficult-to-satisfy desires

label.zh: 先澄清我们承诺的到底是什么，以及不知道哪些后果
label.en: Clarify what was promised and which consequences remain unknown

prompt.zh: 面对一个可以简化的小仪式，你更想问？
prompt.en: A small ritual could be simplified. Which question appeals first?

label.zh: 哪些繁复安排只是刻意维持表象，可以少强求
label.en: Which elaborate arrangements force an appearance and could be reduced

label.zh: 简化后是否仍满足真实需要，同时减少持续追逐的负担
label.en: Whether simplicity meets needs while reducing the burden of continued pursuit

label.zh: 简化是否扩大了参与者自己选择与行动的空间，而不只是由我决定什么更自由
label.en: Whether simplifying opens participants’ possibilities for choice and action rather than letting me decide what freedom should mean for them

label.zh: 对于这些参与者，怎样保留合宜意义而不过与不及
label.en: What preserves appropriate meaning for these participants without excess or deficiency

prompt.zh: 别人邀请你追求一个看起来很精彩的额外目标，你先想？
prompt.en: Someone invites you to pursue an impressive extra goal. What would you consider first?

label.zh: 这个目标是否触动我真正在意的尺度，还是只把别人的成就标准加到自己身上
label.en: Whether this goal challenges standards I genuinely care about or merely adds someone else’s measure of achievement

label.zh: 我现在承担的事是否仍能认真、公正地完成，而不是只想着未来的称赞
label.en: Whether I can still attend carefully and fairly to present responsibilities rather than thinking only of future praise

label.zh: 精彩的标准是什么，有什么理由把它当成自己的目标
label.en: What makes it impressive and why it should become my aim

label.zh: 现有的承诺与相处需要怎样被诚实对待
label.en: How existing commitments and relationships can be treated sincerely

prompt.zh: 一次日常选择需要收尾，你更愿意用哪种问题回顾？
prompt.en: To review an ordinary choice, which question would you use?

label.zh: 我是否认真处理了自己的判断与行动，而未假定能支配所有结果
label.en: Whether I considered my judgment and actions without assuming command of every outcome

label.zh: 我原先声称知道什么，哪些说法经不起追问
label.en: What I claimed to know and which claims did not withstand inquiry

label.zh: 在这件具体事上，我反复练习的做法是否合宜
label.en: Whether the practice I repeated was appropriate in this particular situation

label.zh: 哪些强行推动其实可以放下，让事情少受干预
label.en: Which attempts at forcing could be reduced to leave the situation less constrained

title.zh: 苏格拉底联想：检视我们所说的知道
title.en: Socrates Association: Examining What We Claim to Know

headline.zh: 原典中的一个阅读入口，不是历史人物性格模拟。
headline.en: One reading entrance into a primary text, not a simulation of historical personality.

summary.zh: 本次较常先澄清概念、追问理由与承认未知。这里联想柏拉图笔下的苏格拉底式检视，不判你像历史人物或更聪明。
summary.en: Your choices more often began with meanings, grounds and acknowledged uncertainty. This associates with inquiry in Plato’s portrayal of Socrates rather than historical personality or intelligence.

scoreReading.zh: 18题各选一项，对应阅读联想加1，次数合计18。每题提供九种思路中的四种；九类各出现8次，每个位置2次。未出现的五项不记为拒绝，分母8是曝光次数，不是相似度百分比、人群排名、人格强度或学说赞同率。所有最高计数保留全文，不用名单顺序硬派主副型；全选同一位置会九类各2，九份全部显示。相差一次只是一道选择，不证明显著差异或固定身份。近分可一起读，但不补造混合哲学家。计数是本题组选项的相对分布，一项被选时其他项没有被选，不是九项独立特质测量；时间、情境、熟悉程度与措辞都可能影响回答。新版改变了对象与部分选项，不能把新旧计数直接互认，或解释为思想、道德、人格及能力的进步或退步。
scoreReading.en: Choose one option for all eighteen questions; each adds one count and the total is eighteen. Each question offers four of nine approaches. Every approach appears eight times and twice in each position. Absent options are not counted as rejected. Eight is an exposure denominator rather than a similarity percentage, population rank, personality intensity or proportion of doctrine endorsed. Every highest count retains its full guide without list-order primary or secondary types. Choosing the same position throughout gives two each and displays all nine. A one-choice gap establishes no significant difference or fixed identity. Read close guides without inventing hybrid philosophers. Counts describe relative choices within this set rather than nine independent traits. Time, context, familiarity and wording can affect responses. This edition changes the figures and some options. Old and new counts are not directly interchangeable and cannot establish intellectual, moral, personality or ability progress or decline.

title.zh: 哲学家测试：苏格拉底结果与完整说明
title.en: Socrates Result: Questions, Reasons & Full Guide

description.zh: 本次较常先澄清概念、追问理由与承认未知。这里联想柏拉图笔下的苏格拉底式检视，不判你像历史人物或更聪明。
description.en: Read the Socrates association through knowledge claims, examples and eight comparisons. A full guide without historical personality or intelligence verdicts.

title.zh: 从柏拉图的记述出发
title.en: Beginning with Plato’s portrayal

paragraphs.zh: 《申辩篇》中，苏格拉底在听到神谕后检视那些被认为有知识的人，并区分知道某些技艺与自以为懂得所有重要问题。这段记述为本版“检视知识声称”的阅读联想提供背景；它不是给历史人物做过的人格测量，也不把对话主人公的每句话当作无争议传记。本站只选择这个问题意识，后面的日常例子与题目均为原创，不声称复现整套苏格拉底哲学。
paragraphs.en: In Plato’s Apology, Socrates examines people reputed to possess knowledge and distinguishes expertise in a craft from assuming expertise in every important matter. This portrayal contextualises an association with examining knowledge claims. It supplies neither personality measurements nor an uncontested biography. This edition selects a concern about inquiry rather than reproducing a complete Socratic philosophy. Its contemporary examples and choices are independently written, and no answer is attributed to the historical person.

title.zh: 计数指向一种起手问题
title.en: Counts point to an opening question

paragraphs.zh: 如果这一项最高，比较合适的读法是：在本题提供的选项中，你较常想先问“我们说的到底是什么，有什么依据”。这不表示你永远怀疑、辩论能力强，或比别人更接近真理。原始次数也没有区分认真检视与为了拖延而发问；需要回到具体情境才能讨论。最高并列保留其他起手点，不把它们解释成你内部不同人格之间的争执。
paragraphs.en: A highest count means you more often wanted to begin by clarifying a claim and its grounds among these options. It establishes no permanent scepticism, debating skill or greater access to truth. Counts cannot distinguish careful inquiry from questions used to delay; that requires examining a real situation. Highest ties retain other starting points without interpreting them as competing personalities inside you. A lower count likewise does not establish that you accept claims uncritically.

title.zh: 一次关于公平的讨论
title.en: A discussion about fairness

paragraphs.zh: 设想朋友安排桌游座位，说“按先到顺序就很公平”。你先问，这里的公平是机会一样、等待时间一样，还是让第一次参加的人也能看清规则？当这些意思分开，大家也许发现自己并非对同一个问题争论。你的提问没有自动选出正确方案；有人仍须根据目的与约定作决定。例子的价值在把理由说清，而非把发问次数多当作更好的行为。
paragraphs.en: Suppose a friend assigns seats for a game by arrival time and calls it fair. You might ask whether fairness here means equal chances, equal waiting or ensuring newcomers can see the rules. Distinguishing meanings may reveal that people are discussing different problems. Asking does not automatically identify the right arrangement; a decision still needs purposes and agreements. The example makes reasons clearer rather than treating a larger number of questions as better conduct.

title.zh: 把自己的判断也放进讨论
title.en: Putting your own judgment into the discussion

paragraphs.zh: 可以说“我把公平理解成让新人也有同样机会，所以想先确认座位会不会影响看规则；这是我的理解，你们怎么看”。你既提出问题，也说明自己的理由，让别人能够检视你，而不只是由你检视他们。讨论时间有限时，可以把尚未解决的问题明确留下，再共同决定本次怎么办。结果没有要求你盘问每个人，也没有把停止追问视作放弃思考。
paragraphs.en: You could explain that you understand fairness as giving newcomers an equal chance, then ask whether seating affects access to the rules. Stating your own grounds lets others examine your view instead of making them the only subjects of inquiry. When time is limited, name the unresolved issue and agree what to do now. This reading requires neither interrogating everyone nor treating an end to questioning as abandoning thought. The concrete issue matters more than maintaining a questioning identity.

title.zh: 与其余八个阅读入口比较
title.en: Comparing the other eight reading entrances

paragraphs.zh: 亚里士多德联想更关心在具体处境中形成怎样的合宜做法；孔子联想把学习、反省与相处联系起来。老子联想会检视是否增加了多余强求，伊壁鸠鲁联想会问追求什么及其代价，爱比克泰德联想区分自身判断与外在结果。苏格拉底入口先检视知识和定义，但这些问题可以先后接续，而不是九位哲学家的完整思想彼此互斥。相近计数不能推出哲学流派归属。
paragraphs.en: Aristotle’s entrance concerns appropriate practice in particulars; the Confucius association links learning, reflection and relationships. Laozi prompts examination of unnecessary forcing, Epicurus asks which desires merit pursuit and their costs, and Epictetus distinguishes judgment from external outcomes. This Socrates entrance begins with knowledge and meanings. These questions can follow one another rather than making nine complete philosophical systems mutually exclusive. Close counts cannot assign a philosophical school, and agreeing with one prompt need not endorse an entire thinker.

paragraphs.zh: 尼采入口会把自己正在沿用的尺度也放进问题里，波伏瓦入口关注自己的选择如何与他人的自由相连。马可·奥勒留入口回到眼前的判断与回应；它与爱比克泰德入口有相邻问题，但本版分别取《沉思录》第二卷的当下反省和《手册》开篇的判断与外在事项区分。这里只比较所选提问，不把这些思想写成彼此互斥的完整体系，也不由接近计数判定流派归属。
paragraphs.en: The Nietzsche entrance also questions the standards you maintain, while Beauvoir asks how your choices relate to the freedom of others. Marcus Aurelius returns to present judgment and response. It shares neighbouring questions with Epictetus, but this edition distinguishes reflection in Meditations Book II from the opening Enchiridion’s distinction between judgment and external matters. These comparisons concern selected questions, not mutually exclusive complete systems or philosophical-school assignments from close counts.

title.zh: 熟悉时不追问也合理
title.en: Not questioning every familiar matter

paragraphs.zh: 你可能对某些概念认真追问，却愿意直接按已了解的约定行动；也可能不喜欢本题选项的表达，但在真实讨论中很重视理由。这些都是范围信息，而非需要消除的矛盾。熟悉程度、时间与他人是否愿意讨论，都影响哪种起手点合适。题目没有测哲学知识、记忆、逻辑能力或诚实，也不能从结果判断别人没有反省精神。对标签不认同时，保留具体答案即可。
paragraphs.en: You may examine some concepts carefully while acting directly on an understood agreement, or dislike the wording here while valuing reasons in actual conversations. Such differences define scope rather than contradictions needing resolution. Familiarity, time and others’ willingness to discuss influence which opening fits. These choices assess no philosophical knowledge, memory, logic or honesty, and cannot establish that someone else lacks reflection. If the association feels unhelpful, keep the particular answers without adopting the name.

title.zh: 为一个词写下可检视的意思
title.en: Making one meaning available for examination

paragraphs.zh: 如果愿意，选一个你在轻松讨论中用过的词，例如公平或成功，写下这次具体指什么，以及什么例子会让你修改理解。然后留一行给尚不知道的部分。无需向别人展示，也不必延伸成每天的训练。这是阅读与对话的可选提示，不承诺提高智力、决策能力或人格。若想继续，阅读《申辩篇》相关段落，注意文本的论证语境，而不是只寻找一句适合贴在结果上的名言。
paragraphs.en: If you wish, choose a word used in a relaxed discussion, such as fair or successful, and note its meaning in that instance and an example that might change your account. Leave room for what remains unknown. No sharing or daily training is required. This is an optional reading and conversation prompt without promises about intelligence, decision skill or personality. For further reading, consider the relevant Apology passage in its argumentative context rather than searching only for a quotation to attach to a result.

title.zh: 18题计数、并列与近分
title.en: 18-item counts, ties and close results

paragraphs.zh: 18题各选一项，对应阅读联想加1，次数合计18。每题提供九种思路中的四种；九类各出现8次，每个位置2次。未出现的五项不记为拒绝，分母8是曝光次数，不是相似度百分比、人群排名、人格强度或学说赞同率。所有最高计数保留全文，不用名单顺序硬派主副型；全选同一位置会九类各2，九份全部显示。相差一次只是一道选择，不证明显著差异或固定身份。近分可一起读，但不补造混合哲学家。计数是本题组选项的相对分布，一项被选时其他项没有被选，不是九项独立特质测量；时间、情境、熟悉程度与措辞都可能影响回答。新版改变了对象与部分选项，不能把新旧计数直接互认，或解释为思想、道德、人格及能力的进步或退步。

A one-choice gap establishes no significant difference or fixed identity. Read close guides without inventing hybrid philosophers. Counts describe relative choices within this set rather than nine independent traits. Time, context, familiarity and wording can affect responses. This edition changes the figures and some options. Old and new counts are not directly interchangeable and cannot establish intellectual, moral, personality or ability progress or decline.

title.zh: 原创题本与原典的不同职责
title.en: Original choices and the role of primary texts

paragraphs.zh: 九位是本版选取的哲学阅读入口，不是全体哲学家、完整思想史或心理学九型。苏格拉底依据柏拉图的记述；论语包括孔子及弟子言论；老子是文本传统名，不在本题裁定单一作者生平。原典仅为所选观念提供语境，不验证原创题目、映射、计数或个体解释。所有题目、选项、例子和报告为本站原创，不采用竞品题本标签正文或复制现代译文。计数不鉴定历史人物性格、智力、品德、宗教政治立场、文化身份、健康、关系或职业，不把某一种观念当现实行动命令。
paragraphs.en: These nine are selected reading entrances, not all philosophers, complete intellectual history or a psychological nine-type system. Primary texts contextualise selected ideas without validating original items, mappings, counts or personal interpretations. Questions, options, examples and reports are independently authored without competitor banks, labels or prose or reproduction of modern translations. Counts establish no historical personality, intelligence, morality, religion, politics, cultural identity, health, relationship or career, and no idea becomes a command for real-world action.

title.en: The context of habituation and the mean

paragraphs.en: Book II of the Nicomachean Ethics links character with repeated action and discusses appropriateness in relation to particular people and circumstances. The mean is not an arithmetic average or a rule that every disagreement requires halfway compromise; the text also denies a mean for every kind of action. This edition selects a reading entrance about practising judgment in particulars. Counts measure no virtue and supply no complete answer from Aristotle’s ethics.

title.zh: 重视做法不等于已经做得好
title.en: Valuing practice is not demonstrated excellence

paragraphs.zh: 本次最高计数只表示你较常先考虑某种做法反复实行会形成什么，以及今天的条件是否适合它。它不能证明已经养成习惯、判断准确或道德较高。选择题记录的是你愿意优先想的理由，而不是观察过的行动。一个人可以赞同练习的重要性，却在某个具体任务上需要时间、指导或资源；这些信息不该由一个哲学家名称补出来。
paragraphs.en: A highest count means you more often considered what repeated practices form and whether a practice fits today’s conditions. It does not prove an established habit, accurate judgment or greater morality. Choices record reasons you want to consider rather than observed conduct. Someone may value practice yet need time, guidance or resources in a particular task. A philosopher’s name cannot fill in those missing facts. Lower counts likewise establish no failure to act or develop skills.

title.zh: 合宜不是机械取中间
title.en: Appropriateness is not mechanically splitting the difference

paragraphs.zh: 一次自愿读书活动，有人想讨论十分钟，有人想谈一小时。你可能先问这次材料长度、参与者时间和目标是什么，再决定二十分钟或另开一场，而不是认定三十五分钟必然最合宜。选择有具体理由，之后也能根据实际体验修改。这个例子不保证某个时长最好，只说明不把“折中”当通用答案，也不从一次安排推断一个人的成熟程度。
paragraphs.en: At an optional reading gathering, one person suggests ten minutes and another an hour. You might examine the text, participants’ time and purpose before choosing twenty minutes or another meeting, rather than assuming thirty-five minutes must be appropriate. Reasons concern the case and can change with experience. This example guarantees no ideal duration. It illustrates why compromise is not a universal answer and why one arrangement cannot establish a person’s maturity.

title.zh: 说清行动与理由的关系
title.en: Explaining the relation between practice and reasons

paragraphs.en: You could propose discussing one passage first, seeing whether participants can explain their reasons and then deciding the next meeting’s length. That makes a practice open to observation and revision instead of using an Aristotle label to claim an ability to find balance. You can acknowledge uncertainty and seek relevant experience. Valuing repetition requires neither accepting an unsuitable arrangement nor persisting indefinitely with every problem. A practical proposal should remain tied to the purpose and conditions.

title.en: Cases where a clear rule is appropriate

paragraphs.zh: 有些活动已经有清楚的安全要求或约定，按要求行动并不与关注具体处境矛盾；本版也没有建议把明确禁止的事拿来寻找中间。你可能只在熟悉领域愿意调整做法，在其他地方先学习。这不是判断力退步，而是知识和条件不同。题目不能评价专业能力、工作表现或道德品质，也不支持由较低计数断言某人只空谈、不实践。
paragraphs.en: An activity may already have clear safety requirements or agreements. Following them need not conflict with attending to particulars, and this edition suggests no search for a middle position on an explicitly prohibited act. You might adapt practice only in familiar areas and seek instruction elsewhere. That reflects differences in knowledge and conditions rather than declining judgment. These choices assess no professional skill, work performance or morality and cannot establish that someone with lower counts talks without acting.

paragraphs.zh: 若愿意，回顾一件普通、可修改的小安排：当时目的是什么，哪些条件重要，哪一种做法实际适合？可以记下一个反例，说明换条件后为何要改。无需给自己打德性分或每天坚持记录；这只是阅读后的可选观察。继续读第二卷时，可以注意习惯、选择与相对中道之间的论证关系，不把它简化成“凡事适量”或一张万能生活处方。
paragraphs.en: If you wish, review one ordinary arrangement that can be changed: its purpose, relevant conditions and which practice fitted. Add a counterexample explaining why different conditions would call for revision. No virtue rating or daily record is needed; this is an optional observation following a reading association. In Book II, consider the argument linking habituation, choice and the relative mean rather than reducing it to moderation in everything or a universal prescription for living.

title.zh: 把言论放回《论语》
title.en: Returning the sayings to the Analects

paragraphs.zh: 《论语》开篇把学与实践联系起来，书中也讨论学习与思考的关系，以及怎样在相处中落实所学。它并非只有孔子一人的话：例如每日反省的表述归于曾子，礼与和的那一段归于有子。本站据这些文本选取学习、反省与相处的阅读切面，不把所有句子都署为孔子，也不把古代社会关系直接当成今日生活的指令。
paragraphs.en: The Analects connects learning with practice and examines reflection and conduct in relationships. It includes voices beyond Confucius: the passage about daily self-examination is attributed to Zengzi, while the discussion of ritual and harmony comes from Youzi. This edition selects an angle involving learning, reflection and dealings with others. It neither attributes every saying to Confucius nor turns ancient social arrangements directly into instructions for contemporary life.

title.zh: 选择一种理由，不是取得道德资格
title.en: Choosing a reason rather than earning moral standing

paragraphs.zh: 如果这一项最高，你在本题里较常把“我怎样学习、守约和回应他人”放在前面。它不认证你有礼、可靠或值得信任，更不判断是否孝顺、是否符合某种文化身份。表面礼貌与真诚相处可能不同，原始次数无法替你区分实际行为。对这些问题感兴趣也不等于赞同传统的一切安排；你可以一边重视反省，一边对具体习俗提出不同意见。
paragraphs.en: A highest count means questions about learning, agreements and responses to others more often came first in this set. It certifies no courtesy, reliability or trustworthiness and establishes no filial conduct or cultural identity. Counts cannot distinguish surface politeness from sincere conduct. Interest in these questions also does not endorse every traditional arrangement. You may value reflection while disagreeing with particular customs. Lower counts establish no disrespect or failure to care about relationships.

title.zh: 共同学习的一次小约定
title.en: A small agreement about learning together

paragraphs.zh: 你与朋友约好各读一小段再讨论。到了时间，你发现自己没有认真看，便说明情况，问是否改成一起读，而不是用漂亮的评论遮过去。这里的阅读联想关注把学习与守信落实在相处中；它不是判断你是否好人，也没有说一次迟误就破坏品格。朋友可能希望改日再谈，双方仍可根据实际时间商量。古典观念给出提问方向，具体约定由当事人决定。
paragraphs.en: You agree to read a passage before meeting a friend but realise you have not attended to it. You explain that and ask about reading together instead of disguising it with polished commentary. This association concerns linking learning and trustworthiness in a relationship. It neither judges goodness nor treats one delay as damaged character. Your friend may prefer another day, and the arrangement remains open to discussion. A classical idea supplies a question while participants decide the actual agreement.

title.zh: 礼貌里可以有真实分歧
title.en: Courtesy can include actual disagreement

paragraphs.zh: 可以说“我知道这个安排用了很久，但这次我有一个不同理由，想先说明”，而不是为了符合标签始终附和。你也可以问对方怎样理解这项约定，哪些部分能调整。表达分歧时不需要通过本测试证明自己有礼，也不必把不同意见解释成背离关系。对他人的时间、回应与拒绝保持具体商量，比把任何一方定为传统型或不尊重的人更有帮助。
paragraphs.en: You can acknowledge that an arrangement is long-standing and then explain a different reason instead of agreeing to fit a label. Ask how the other person understands the agreement and which parts can change. No test result is needed to certify courtesy before disagreeing, and disagreement need not signify abandoning a relationship. Discuss time, responses and refusal concretely rather than naming one party traditional and the other disrespectful. The reading association grants neither person authority over the other.

title.zh: 与另外八种起手点比较
title.en: Comparing the other eight openings

paragraphs.zh: 亚里士多德入口也关注反复实践，本站重点却放在具体处境的合宜判断；孔子入口把学习反省与相处联系起来。苏格拉底先检视定义和声称知道的事，老子检视多余强求，伊壁鸠鲁关注欲望与追求的代价，爱比克泰德分开自身判断和结果。九个切面可以共同出现，不能据此认定中西文化谁更重关系或理性，更不能把一个国家的人全部归入某项。

When reading the Analects further, attend to speakers, conversational contexts and the relation between learning and reflection rather than making an isolated saying a requirement for every situation.

title.zh: 减少干预是一条可检视的思路
title.en: Reduced intervention as an examinable approach

title.en: Giving a conversation fewer prescriptions

paragraphs.zh: 读书活动原本只约定一个时段，后来又加了必须发言的次数、固定句式和连续签到。你想先问，这些安排是不是正在遮住大家想讨论什么；也许保留时长与基本相处约定，去掉几条展示参与的要求就够了。这个例子不证明所有规则有害，更不主张取消安全和必要边界。它只是检视某些为理想样子而增加的控制，是否服务了当初的目的。
paragraphs.en: A reading gathering begins with an agreed time, then adds speaking quotas, prescribed phrases and attendance streaks. You might ask whether these additions obscure what people want to discuss. Keeping a duration and basic agreements while removing some displays of participation may suffice. This establishes no harm from every rule and calls for no removal of safety requirements or necessary boundaries. It examines whether control added to achieve an ideal appearance serves the original purpose.

title.en: Giving reasons for doing less

paragraphs.en: You could propose keeping an ending time while trying one meeting without a three-sentence quota, then reviewing whether the quota was needed. That identifies a particular intervention, retains relevant arrangements and permits revision rather than rejecting all rules under a Laozi label. paragraphs.zh: 遇到该处理的具体问题，你可以提出清楚步骤、寻求帮助或遵守必要要求；这不需要与本次结果冲突。活动条件不同，少干预也有不同含义。题目没有测拖延、主动性、压力、健康或宗教实践，不能把没有采取某个行动当作领悟无为，更不能把较低计数解释为好强或不懂生活。反例让阅读联想保持有限，而非逼你为一个名称改变实际需要。

paragraphs.en: The Letter to Menoeceus distinguishes desires and considers why not every pleasure should be chosen or every discomfort immediately avoided. This edition uses that as a reading entrance about what to pursue and what follows, without reducing Epicurus to luxury or asceticism. The ancient ethical context supplies neither dietary, medical nor psychological advice here. These choices do not make a selected philosophical idea a required formula for contemporary life.

title.zh: 看的是起手考虑的理由
title.en: Reading the reason considered first

paragraphs.en: A highest count means you more often first considered satisfaction alongside further wants, attention or burdens among these options. It proves no greater contentment, happiness, frugality or capacity to enjoy life. Simplicity may reflect limited time or materials rather than a philosophical position, while complexity need not imply discontent. Raw counts assess neither quality of life nor control of desires and offer no comparison of whose life is more worthwhile. They retain a starting reason rather than an achievement.

title.zh: 一个额外活动是否值得
title.en: Whether an extra activity is worth choosing

paragraphs.zh: 周末已经约好一段轻松散步，又出现一个很有吸引力的小活动。你可能先问，加入后的乐趣是否值得赶路、反复查看通知和压缩原有休息；也可能发现自己确实愿意加入。重点不是答案必须少做，而是把追求与后续影响一起考虑。朋友选择不同也不表示谁更有智慧；各自时间、兴趣与安排不同，足以使同一活动有不同意义。
paragraphs.en: A relaxed walk is already planned when another appealing small activity appears. You might consider whether its enjoyment is worth travel, repeated notifications and reduced open time, and may still decide to join. The point is not that less is always correct, but that pursuit and consequences enter the same consideration. A friend choosing differently demonstrates no difference in wisdom. Available time, interests and arrangements can make the same activity mean different things.

title.zh: 说清想要与不想增加的部分
title.en: Naming the enjoyment and the added burden

paragraphs.zh: 可以说“我喜欢这个活动，但今天不想再安排赶路，所以保留原来的散步”，也可以说“我愿意多花一点时间，想试一次”。两句话都比“我是伊壁鸠鲁型，所以只过简单生活”更能说明具体选择。你不必贬低别人的乐趣，也不需要为自己的需要寻找哲学家背书。对后果尚不清楚时，可以承认未知，而不是保证某一种选择必然令人满足。
paragraphs.en: You can explain enjoying an activity while declining extra travel today, or choose to spend more time and try it. Either states a practical choice more clearly than a type-based rule about living simply. There is no need to belittle another person’s enjoyment or recruit a philosopher to legitimise your needs. When consequences are unclear, acknowledge that uncertainty rather than guaranteeing satisfaction from a particular choice. This association assigns no preferred lifestyle to everyone.

title.en: Distinguishing pursuit, intervention and knowledge

paragraphs.en: Laozi’s entrance may also lead to simpler arrangements, but here it examines unnecessary forcing. The Epicurus entrance concerns desires, satisfaction and what follows. These comparisons concern selected questions, not mutually exclusive complete systems or philosophical-school assignments from close counts.

title.en: Willing effort need not conflict with satisfaction

paragraphs.en: If you wish, take an ordinary optional activity and ask what you want from it and what else it asks of you. Worthwhile and uncertain are both possible answers, without a happiness score or lifestyle change. This observation promises no health or mood improvement. In further reading, follow how distinctions among desires and choices about pleasure and discomfort fit the argument rather than seeking only a slogan that simplicity is best. Ancient food examples supply no contemporary bodily advice.

title.en: Beginning with the Enchiridion’s distinction

paragraphs.en: The Enchiridion opens by distinguishing judgment, desire and action from external matters such as property and reputation, and examines responses to appearances. This contextualises a question about personal choice versus external outcomes. It does not claim that contemporary emotions or behaviour can all be controlled at will. title.en: Distinguishing is not guaranteeing control

paragraphs.zh: 你认真做了一个小展示，却没有得到预想的回应。你可以回看自己的说明是否清楚、材料是否准备好，同时承认不能保证每个人喜欢；需要反馈时，仍然可以问。这个区分不是让你认定外部结果不重要，也不是说失望是判断错误。它帮助把可继续考虑的部分分开讨论，最后是否调整展示、邀请谁回应，仍由具体目的与条件决定。
paragraphs.en: You prepare a small display and receive an unexpected response. You can review the clarity of your explanation and preparation while acknowledging that not everyone’s approval is guaranteed, and still request feedback. This distinction does not make outcomes unimportant or disappointment a mistaken judgment. It separates matters for consideration. Whether to revise the display and whose feedback to request remains a practical choice informed by purposes and circumstances rather than a command attached to this result.

title.zh: 表达努力，也承认结果的不确定
title.en: Stating effort and uncertainty together

paragraphs.zh: 可以说“我会把说明补清楚，也想听你的建议，但不能要求你一定喜欢”，而不是“别人的反应不归我管，所以我不听”。前一句区分了行动、邀请与对方的决定，仍给讨论留下空间。你也可以直接说自己失望并请求陪伴，结果不要求压下感受。边界、必要帮助和现实责任应单独讨论，不由一个哲学阅读标签替你或别人取消。
paragraphs.en: You might explain that you will clarify your account and welcome suggestions without requiring approval. That differs from using lack of control as a reason to ignore feedback. It distinguishes an action, an invitation and another person’s decision while leaving discussion possible. You can also express disappointment and ask for company; suppressing feelings is not required. Boundaries, necessary help and actual responsibilities need separate consideration rather than cancellation by a philosophical reading label.

title.zh: 与顺势、欲望和实践分别比较
title.en: Comparing intervention, desire and practice

paragraphs.zh: 老子入口检视是否过度强求事情，爱比克泰德入口区分自己的判断与外在结果；少做不等于更符合后者。伊壁鸠鲁入口衡量追求与代价，苏格拉底入口检视知识与定义，亚里士多德入口关注具体合宜与反复实践，孔子入口关注学习反省与相处。它们是本版选取的提问角度，不是每位哲学家的全部思想，也不把某一项定义为更理性、更健康或更成熟。
paragraphs.en: Laozi’s entrance examines excessive forcing; Epictetus distinguishes judgment and external outcomes, so doing less is not automatically a closer fit. Epicurus weighs pursuits and consequences, Socrates knowledge and meanings, Aristotle appropriate repeated practice, and Confucius learning, reflection and relationships. These are selected questions rather than the entirety of each thinker’s work. No entrance is defined as more rational, healthy or mature, and tied counts retain different questions without proving that all their underlying doctrines coincide.

paragraphs.zh: 尼采入口会把自己正在沿用的尺度也放进问题里，波伏瓦入口关注自己的选择如何与他人的自由相连。马可·奥勒留入口回到眼前的判断与回应；它与爱比克泰德入口有相邻问题，但本版分别取《沉思录》第二卷的当下反省和《手册》开篇的判断与外在事项区分。这里只比较所选提问，不把这些思想写成彼此互斥的完整体系，也不由接近计数判定流派归属。
paragraphs.en: The Nietzsche entrance also questions the standards you maintain, while Beauvoir asks how your choices relate to the freedom of others. Marcus Aurelius returns to present judgment and response. It shares neighbouring questions with Epictetus, but this edition distinguishes reflection in Meditations Book II from the opening Enchiridion’s distinction between judgment and external matters. These comparisons concern selected questions, not mutually exclusive complete systems or philosophical-school assignments from close counts.

title.zh: 关心结果与这一区分相容
title.en: Caring about outcomes can coexist with the distinction

paragraphs.zh: 你可以认真关心朋友的回应、考试结果或共同活动是否顺利，同时承认无法保证一切。某个外部条件可以通过协作改变，也不因为“不完全由我决定”就该放弃。题目没有评估焦虑、抑郁、创伤、心理韧性或控制能力；不能从较低计数断言情绪化，也不能用较高计数证明不需要支持。若标签使你感到必须责备自己，可以不用名称，只保留实际有用的那个问题。
paragraphs.en: You can care about a friend’s response or a shared activity while acknowledging that not everything is guaranteed. Collaboration may change an external condition; lacking complete control is no reason to abandon it. These choices assess no anxiety, depression, trauma, resilience or control capacity. Lower counts establish no emotionality, and higher counts establish no lack of need for support. If the label encourages self-blame, set it aside and retain only a question that helps in the actual situation.

title.zh: 把一个问题分开写
title.en: Separating one question into parts

paragraphs.zh: 若愿意，回顾一件普通小事，把自己接下来愿意做的选择写在一边，把不能保证的回应写在另一边，再留一行给需要他人帮助的部分。也可以不写，或发现两个部分并不容易分清。没有必须做到冷静的考核，也没有心理改善承诺。继续读《手册》开篇时，留意它如何论证这一区分，与自己今天可使用的有限提问之间保持距离，不把古代断言直接当心理事实。
paragraphs.en: If you wish, review an ordinary matter by separating a next choice you want to make from a response you cannot guarantee, leaving room for needed help. You may skip writing or find the boundary unclear. There is no requirement to achieve calm and no psychological improvement promise. In further reading, examine how the opening Enchiridion argues for its distinction while keeping it separate from the limited question you find useful today. An ancient assertion does not automatically become a psychological fact.

title.zh: 18题计数、并列与近分
title.en: 18-item counts, ties and close results

paragraphs.zh: 18题各选一项，对应阅读联想加1，次数合计18。每题提供九种思路中的四种；九类各出现8次，每个位置2次。未出现的五项不记为拒绝，分母8是曝光次数，不是相似度百分比、人群排名、人格强度或学说赞同率。所有最高计数保留全文，不用名单顺序硬派主副型；全选同一位置会九类各2，九份全部显示。相差一次只是一道选择，不证明显著差异或固定身份。近分可一起读，但不补造混合哲学家。计数是本题组选项的相对分布，一项被选时其他项没有被选，不是九项独立特质测量；时间、情境、熟悉程度与措辞都可能影响回答。新版改变了对象与部分选项，不能把新旧计数直接互认，或解释为思想、道德、人格及能力的进步或退步。
paragraphs.en: Choose one option for all eighteen questions; each adds one count and the total is eighteen. Each question offers four of nine approaches. Every approach appears eight times and twice in each position. Absent options are not counted as rejected. Eight is an exposure denominator rather than a similarity percentage, population rank, personality intensity or proportion of doctrine endorsed. Every highest count retains its full guide without list-order primary or secondary types. Choosing the same position throughout gives two each and displays all nine. A one-choice gap establishes no significant difference or fixed identity. Read close guides without inventing hybrid philosophers. Counts describe relative choices within this set rather than nine independent traits. Time, context, familiarity and wording can affect responses. This edition changes the figures and some options. Old and new counts are not directly interchangeable and cannot establish intellectual, moral, personality or ability progress or decline.

title.zh: 原创题本与原典的不同职责
title.en: Original choices and the role of primary texts

paragraphs.zh: 九位是本版选取的哲学阅读入口，不是全体哲学家、完整思想史或心理学九型。苏格拉底依据柏拉图的记述；论语包括孔子及弟子言论；老子是文本传统名，不在本题裁定单一作者生平。原典仅为所选观念提供语境，不验证原创题目、映射、计数或个体解释。所有题目、选项、例子和报告为本站原创，不采用竞品题本标签正文或复制现代译文。计数不鉴定历史人物性格、智力、品德、宗教政治立场、文化身份、健康、关系或职业，不把某一种观念当现实行动命令。
paragraphs.en: These nine are selected reading entrances, not all philosophers, complete intellectual history or a psychological nine-type system. Socrates is approached through Plato; the Analects includes Confucius and disciples; Laozi names a textual tradition without this quiz deciding a single author’s biography. Primary texts contextualise selected ideas without validating original items, mappings, counts or personal interpretations. Questions, options, examples and reports are independently authored without competitor banks, labels or prose or reproduction of modern translations. Counts establish no historical personality, intelligence, morality, religion, politics, cultural identity, health, relationship or career, and no idea becomes a command for real-world action.

title.zh: 尼采联想：重估自己的尺度
title.en: Nietzsche Association: Reconsidering Your Standards

headline.zh: 把自己正在维护的标准也放进问题里。
headline.en: Include the standards you maintain in the question.

summary.zh: 本次较常先追问：我正在追求什么，哪些尺度只是沿用，又有哪些值得重新承担？这里关联尼采文本中的自我超越问题，不判你像真实尼采或比别人更强。
summary.en: Your choices more often questioned what you pursue, which standards you inherit and which you would choose anew. This associates with self-overcoming in a selected Nietzsche text, not resemblance to Nietzsche or superiority over other people.

scoreReading.zh: 尼采选项出现8次，四个位置各2次；每次选择加1，18题完整后显示九类计数。全部最高并列保留。计数不测自我超越能力、勇气或思想深度，也不代表赞同尼采全部思想。新版改变了选项与对象，不与旧版计数直接互认。
scoreReading.en: Nietzsche options appear eight times, twice in each position; each selection adds one count. Complete all 18 questions for nine counts and every highest tie. Counts measure no capacity for self-overcoming, courage or depth of thought and endorse no whole doctrine. Changed options and figures prevent direct comparison with the previous edition.

title.zh: 从“自我超越”的文本问题出发
title.en: Beginning with the question of self-overcoming

paragraphs.zh: 《查拉图斯特拉如是说》第二部“自我超越”把生命、意欲和价值的不断超越联系起来，文本不只是劝人完成更多目标。本站只取一个有限的当代阅读问题：自己所维护的尺度能否也被重新检视？这不是把复杂学说改写成励志训练，更不借原典证明原创选择题能测一个人的精神强弱。
paragraphs.en: Self-Surpassing in Part II of Thus Spake Zarathustra connects life, willing and the surpassing of values rather than merely urging more completed goals. This edition takes one limited contemporary question: can the standards we maintain themselves be reconsidered? It does not turn the doctrine into motivational training or use the passage to validate a test of personal strength.

title.zh: 计数指向重新选择尺度的提问
title.en: Counts point to a question about choosing standards anew

paragraphs.zh: 较高计数只说明，这些选项中你较常先考虑自己的追求和评价标准是否仍值得承担。它不能证明你独立、叛逆、创造力强或已经完成自我超越。你也许只对某一个旧习惯起疑，而在其他方面仍愿守住熟悉的标准。重估之后继续原来的选择，也可以是有理由的回答。
paragraphs.en: A higher count means you more often began by asking whether your pursuits and standards remained worth choosing. It proves no independence, rebelliousness, creativity or accomplished self-overcoming. You may question one habit while retaining familiar standards elsewhere. Reconsideration can also lead you to continue an existing choice for reasons you can now state.

title.zh: 一个看起来很精彩的额外目标
title.en: An impressive additional goal

paragraphs.zh: 朋友邀请你参加一项很受称赞的活动。这个阅读入口会先问：吸引我的是实际想探索的东西，还是“做得越多才越值得肯定”的旧尺度？你可以选择参加、谢绝或缩小投入。例子的重点是把评价标准说清，不是把拒绝集体活动当成更高级，也不是把劳累证明为成长。
paragraphs.en: A friend invites you to a widely admired activity. This entrance first asks whether you want to explore it or are following an old standard that doing more makes you more worthy. Joining, declining or limiting your involvement can all remain available. The point is to name the standard, not to rank refusal above participation or turn exhaustion into evidence of growth.

title.zh: 给重新选择留下可说明的理由
title.en: Giving a renewed choice an account

paragraphs.zh: 可以这样表达：“我以前把这件事当作进步的证明，现在想重新说明它为什么值得做。”接着说出愿意承担的具体方向和现实限制，而不是只宣布旧标准都无意义。若选择影响同伴，还需处理已作约定与对方的不同意见。原典联想不授予忽略别人、撕毁承诺或为伤害辩护的资格。
paragraphs.en: You might say that you previously treated an activity as proof of progress and now want to explain why it deserves your effort. Name the direction you would choose and its real limits rather than merely dismissing every old standard. Choices affecting companions still involve agreements and differing views. A reading association supplies no exemption from responsibility or justification for harming others.

title.zh: 与其余八个阅读入口比较
title.en: Comparing the other eight reading entrances

paragraphs.zh: 苏格拉底入口先问定义与依据；本版尼采入口把自己的评价尺度也纳入重估。亚里士多德关注具体合宜与反复实践，孔子关注学习反省与相处。老子检视多余强求，伊壁鸠鲁辨别追求及代价。爱比克泰德区分判断与结果，马可·奥勒留关注当下合宜回应；波伏瓦关注自己的计划是否也为他人留下自由。这些是本站有限提问切面，不是历史学说互斥表，也不把尼采解释为只顾自己。
paragraphs.en: Socrates begins with meanings and grounds; this Nietzsche entrance also reconsiders the standards used to value a choice. Aristotle concerns appropriate repeated practice and Confucius reflective learning in relationships. Laozi examines unnecessary forcing, while Epicurus weighs pursuits and consequences. Epictetus distinguishes judgment and outcomes; Marcus Aurelius attends to the present response. Beauvoir asks whether a project leaves others possibilities for freedom. These are limited questions authored for this edition, not an exclusion chart of historical doctrines or an account of Nietzsche as simply ignoring others.

title.zh: 不改变不等于没有反省
title.en: Keeping a choice can follow reflection

paragraphs.zh: 一个熟悉标准可能仍有充分理由，例如约定好的质量要求或你确实重视的学习方向。不需要为显得敢于超越而不断推翻自己。条件有限、需要休息或暂时不想改变，也不能由低计数判成软弱。题本不评估资源、意志、人生处境或改变是否可行。
paragraphs.en: A familiar standard may remain well founded, such as an agreed quality requirement or a direction of study you value. You do not need continual reversal to appear capable of surpassing yourself. Limited resources, a need for rest or no present wish to change cannot be labelled weakness from a low count. The set evaluates neither your circumstances nor the feasibility of change.

title.zh: 回顾一个低风险的小标准
title.en: Revisiting one low-stakes standard

paragraphs.zh: 愿意时，写下一个日常自我要求，例如“空闲也必须有成果”。旁边记下它从哪里来、目前帮到什么、又妨碍什么，再写一种你愿意承担的替代说法。也可以决定保留原标准。无需实际改变工作、关系或重要安排；若继续阅读“自我超越”，留意其价值问题，不把文本读成永不休息的命令。
paragraphs.en: If you wish, note an everyday demand on yourself, such as requiring free time to produce an outcome. Consider where it came from, what it currently helps and what it obstructs, then formulate an alternative you would choose. Keeping the original is also possible. No change to work, relationships or important arrangements is required. Further reading can attend to the question of values rather than an instruction never to rest.

title.zh: 18题、8次曝光与全部并列
title.en: 18 questions, eight exposures and every tie

paragraphs.zh: 18题各选一项，合计18次；九类各出现8次，四个位置各2次。每选一次加1，未出现不算拒绝，8不是相似度百分比。全部最高并列完整显示；固定选同一位置会九类各2次。差一次不证明显著差异或思想身份，选择间也非九项独立特质。新版更换了对象与部分选项，不能把新旧计数直接解释为成长或退步。
paragraphs.en: Eighteen single choices total 18 counts. Each of nine approaches appears eight times, twice in every position. Selections add one; absent options are not rejected and eight is not a similarity percentage. Every highest tie appears in full; choosing one position throughout gives two each. A one-choice difference establishes no significant difference or intellectual identity. These are not nine independent traits, and changed options prevent old and new counts from measuring progress or decline.

title.zh: 阅读联想与人物人格的边界
title.en: A reading association and historical personality

paragraphs.zh: 本结果只选取明确段落中的一个问题，不是尼采全部思想、真实人格或政治立场的摘要。原典不验证本站原创题目、映射或个体解释，本文也不复制现代译文。结果不测智力、创造力、道德、心理健康、文化身份或职业，不证明你属于某个流派；可以保留一个有用问题而不接受名称。
paragraphs.en: This result takes one question from a selected passage, not Nietzsche’s entire thought, historical personality or politics. The text validates no original questionnaire mapping or personal interpretation, and modern translations are not reproduced. The result measures no intelligence, creativity, morality, mental health, cultural identity or career fit and assigns no philosophical school. A useful question can be retained without adopting the name.

title.zh: 尼采联想结果：自我超越与重估尺度
title.en: Nietzsche Result: Self-Overcoming and Reconsidered Standards

description.zh: 阅读尼采联想的原典语境、当代例子、八入口比较和完整计分说明。只讨论重估自己尺度的阅读问题，不模拟尼采人格或测思想能力。
description.en: Read the Nietzsche association through a selected self-overcoming passage, examples, eight comparisons and clear scoring, without personality or ability claims.

title.zh: 波伏瓦联想：彼此自由与处境中的选择
title.en: Simone de Beauvoir Association: Freedom with Others

headline.zh: 自己的计划，也给他人留下选择与行动的可能。
headline.en: Consider whether your project leaves others possibilities to choose and act.

summary.zh: 本次较常先问：我的选择会怎样影响别人继续选择和行动的空间？这里联想波伏瓦关于个人自由与他人的讨论，不判断你更善良、政治上属于哪一派或像真实人物。
summary.en: Your choices more often began with how your actions affect others’ possibilities for choice and action. This associates with Beauvoir’s discussion of freedom and others, not moral superiority, political affiliation or resemblance to the historical person.

scoreReading.zh: 波伏瓦选项出现8次，四个位置各2次；每次选择加1，18题完整后显示九类计数和全部最高并列。计数不是自由程度、同理心或道德分数，不代表赞同完整学说，也不能与旧版计数直接比较。
scoreReading.en: Beauvoir options appear eight times, twice in each position. Each selection adds one count; completing 18 questions shows nine counts and every highest tie. Counts measure no freedom, empathy or morality, endorse no whole doctrine and cannot be compared directly with the previous edition.

title.zh: 个人自由与他人的具体联系
title.en: The concrete relation between personal freedom and others

paragraphs.zh: 《模糊性的伦理学》第二部分末部及结论，把自己的自由与他人的自由联系起来，也承认人彼此分离、计划可能冲突。本站选取的问题是：一个由我选择的计划，是否也为别人留下继续选择和行动的可能？这不是把伦理学缩成讨好或一致同意，更不是由问卷替你裁定现实冲突中的正确答案。
paragraphs.en: The closing discussion of Part II and the conclusion of The Ethics of Ambiguity connect one’s freedom with others’ freedom while acknowledging separate people and conflicting projects. This edition asks whether a chosen project leaves others possibilities to choose and act. That is not a formula for pleasing everyone or securing agreement, and the questionnaire cannot adjudicate a real ethical conflict.

title.zh: 计数指向参与者的真实选择
title.en: Counts point to participants’ actual possibilities

paragraphs.zh: 较高计数只表示你在本题中较常先注意别人的选择余地、计划与回应，而不只看自己的安排是否完成。它不证明你更公正、合作能力更强或从不压迫别人。你可能在某件事上愿意扩大讨论，在另一件事上需要明确界限；这些具体条件比人物名称更重要。
paragraphs.en: A higher count means you more often first considered others’ room for choice, their projects and responses rather than only whether your arrangement succeeded. It proves no fairness, cooperative skill or absence of oppressive behaviour. You may open discussion in one matter and need a firm boundary in another. Those particular conditions matter more than a name.

title.zh: 共同计划因天气而改变
title.en: A shared plan changes with the weather

paragraphs.zh: 你为朋友准备了户外活动，天气变化后很想让大家接受自己的替代方案。这个入口会问：我的投入是否被当成别人必须跟随的理由？可以说明想法，也把留在家、另约时间或提出其他安排留给对方。重点是实际选择空间，不是假装没有自己的偏好，更不是要求每个方案最后都一致。
paragraphs.en: You prepared an outdoor activity and now want friends to accept your replacement plan. This entrance asks whether your investment has become a reason they must follow. You can state your preference while leaving staying home, rescheduling or proposing something else available. The issue is actual room for choice, not pretending to have no preference or requiring eventual agreement.

title.zh: 同时说明自己的选择与他人的余地
title.en: Stating a choice without deciding for everyone

paragraphs.zh: 可以说：“这是我愿意做的方案，但我不把你参加当作已经同意。你还有哪些想法？”随后认真处理不同回答和共同资源的限制，而不只把“你可以拒绝”说成礼貌口头禅。若别人不愿参加，你仍可决定自己的下一步。尊重选择不等于负责实现对方全部愿望。
paragraphs.en: You might explain what you would like to do without assuming another person has agreed to join, then ask what they have in mind. Attend to the answer and shared constraints rather than using permission to decline as a polite formula. Someone’s refusal still leaves you choices about your own next step. Respecting choice does not mean fulfilling every wish.

title.zh: 与其余八个阅读入口比较
title.en: Comparing the other eight reading entrances

paragraphs.zh: 苏格拉底入口澄清理由，亚里士多德关注具体合宜，孔子关注学习与相处；本版波伏瓦入口把参与者继续选择和行动的可能放在前面。老子问是否多余强求，伊壁鸠鲁问追求及代价。尼采入口重估自己的尺度；爱比克泰德区分判断与结果，马可·奥勒留关注眼前合宜回应。它们都可能涉及他人，本版只是选择不同起手问题，不能把波伏瓦化约成讨好、把其他思想说成漠视他人。
paragraphs.en: Socrates clarifies grounds, Aristotle considers appropriate practice and Confucius reflective learning in relationships. This Beauvoir entrance foregrounds participants’ continuing possibilities for choice and action. Laozi questions unnecessary forcing and Epicurus weighs pursuits and consequences. Nietzsche reconsiders standards; Epictetus distinguishes judgment and outcomes, while Marcus Aurelius attends to the present response. All can concern others. The edition selects different opening questions rather than reducing Beauvoir to pleasing people or depicting the other thinkers as indifferent to them.

title.zh: 界限与分歧仍然可以存在
title.en: Boundaries and disagreement can remain

paragraphs.zh: 一次真实拒绝可能让你失望，你也可以拒绝对方提出的安排。不是每个分歧都靠增加选项解决，现实的资源、责任和不对等关系也不能只靠一句“自由选择”消失。低计数不证明自私，高计数不免除检查实际影响。题本没有评估冲突中的风险或替任何人作伦理裁决。
paragraphs.en: A real refusal may disappoint you, and you can also decline another person’s proposal. More options do not solve every disagreement, while resources, responsibilities and unequal conditions do not disappear when someone says choice is free. Low counts establish no selfishness; high counts do not remove the need to examine effects. The set assesses no conflict risks or ethical verdict.

title.zh: 画出一次小安排里的选择
title.en: Noticing choices within a small arrangement

paragraphs.zh: 愿意时，回顾一个低风险的共同安排：你选择了什么，其他人可以选择什么，哪些限制其实还没有说清？把自己的偏好与替别人作的决定分开记录，不必联系任何人或重新谈判。继续阅读原典时，留意自由如何落实在具体处境，而不只寻找一句可以替自己赢得争论的话。
paragraphs.en: If you wish, recall a low-stakes shared arrangement: what did you choose, what could others choose, and which constraints remained unclear? Distinguish your preference from decisions made for someone else. No contact or renegotiation is required. Further reading can attend to freedom in particular situations rather than supplying a sentence with which to win an argument.

title.zh: 18题、8次曝光与全部并列
title.en: 18 questions, eight exposures and every tie

paragraphs.zh: 18题各选一项，合计18次；九类各出现8次，四个位置各2次。每选一次加1，未出现不算拒绝，8不是相似度百分比。全部最高并列完整显示；固定选同一位置会九类各2次。差一次不证明显著差异或思想身份，选择间也非九项独立特质。新版更换了对象与部分选项，不能把新旧计数直接解释为道德或人格变化。
paragraphs.en: Eighteen single choices total 18 counts. Each of nine approaches appears eight times, twice in every position. Selections add one; absent options are not rejected and eight is not a similarity percentage. Every highest tie appears in full; choosing one position throughout gives two each. A one-choice difference establishes no significant difference or intellectual identity. These are not nine independent traits, and changed options prevent old and new counts from measuring moral or personality change.

title.zh: 有限伦理阅读，不是道德鉴定
title.en: A limited ethical reading, not a moral assessment

paragraphs.zh: 本结果只选取《模糊性的伦理学》的明确段落，不概括波伏瓦全部思想或真实人格。原典不验证本站原创题项、映射与计数，本文不复制现代译文。结果不判断性别身份、政治立场、同理心、智力、道德、心理健康或职业，不替现实中的人决定怎样才算自由。可以读一个问题而不接受人物联想。
paragraphs.en: The result selects passages from The Ethics of Ambiguity rather than summarising Beauvoir’s whole thought or historical personality. The text validates no original items, mappings or counts, and modern translations are not reproduced. Results assess no gender identity, politics, empathy, intelligence, morality, mental health or career fit and do not decide what freedom must mean for someone in a real situation. Reading the question requires no adoption of the association.

title.zh: 波伏瓦联想结果：彼此自由与具体选择
title.en: Simone de Beauvoir Result: Freedom and Choices with Others

description.zh: 阅读波伏瓦联想的原典语境、共同计划例子、八入口比较和完整计分。关注彼此选择的可能，不给道德分数或模拟历史人物人格。
description.en: Read the Beauvoir association through freedom with others, a shared-plan example, eight comparisons and scoring, without moral or personality ratings.

title.zh: 马可·奥勒留联想：认真回应眼前
title.en: Marcus Aurelius Association: Attending to the Present Response

headline.zh: 检视此刻的判断，再选择怎样与人共处。
headline.en: Examine the present judgment and consider how to act with others.

summary.zh: 本次较常把注意转回眼前的判断、正在承担的事和对他人的回应。这里关联《沉思录》第二卷的有限阅读问题，不证明冷静、自律或任何情绪都能由意志控制。
summary.en: Your choices more often returned to present judgment, the matter at hand and your response to others. This associates with a limited question in Meditations Book II, not proof of calm, discipline or voluntary command over every emotion.

scoreReading.zh: 马可·奥勒留选项出现8次，四个位置各2次；每次选择加1，18题完整后显示九类计数及全部最高并列。它不是镇定、抗压或自律分数，也不表示你像历史人物。新版选择集合不同，原版计数不能直接当作前测比较。
scoreReading.en: Marcus Aurelius options appear eight times, twice in each position. Each selection adds one count; completing 18 questions shows nine counts and every highest tie. This is no calmness, resilience or discipline score and establishes no historical resemblance. The changed choice set cannot directly use previous counts as a pretest.

title.zh: 从《沉思录》第二卷的自我提醒出发
title.en: Beginning with reminders in Meditations Book II

paragraphs.zh: 《沉思录》第二卷开篇把与他人合作放入自我提醒，随后谈认真处理眼前行动，并留意自己的判断。本站取其中一个有限入口：外部情况不如预期时，我现在怎样理解并回应？这是对特定文本的阅读联想，不是从古代段落推出一个已验证的情绪管理方法，也不要求赞同其全部自然观和宗教观。
paragraphs.en: Book II of Meditations begins with reminders about cooperation and later attends to present action and one’s own judgment. This edition takes one limited entrance: when circumstances disappoint me, how am I interpreting and responding now? It is a reading association, not a validated emotional-management method derived from an ancient passage, and requires no endorsement of the text’s entire cosmology or religion.

title.zh: 计数指向当前回应的提问
title.en: Counts point to a question about the current response

paragraphs.zh: 较高计数只说明你较常先考虑眼前可以怎样认真、公正地回应，而不是只追逐称赞或让不满替你决定。它不证明你总能平静、没有焦虑或更擅长承受压力。感到生气、失望和需要帮助，都可以与检视判断同时存在；这18道选择没有测情绪调节表现。
paragraphs.en: A higher count means you more often first considered how to respond carefully and fairly now rather than orienting only toward praise or letting dissatisfaction determine the next step. It proves no calmness, absence of anxiety or stress tolerance. Anger, disappointment and needing help can coexist with examining a judgment. These 18 choices do not assess emotional-regulation performance.

title.zh: 一次没有得到预期配合的讨论
title.en: A discussion without the cooperation you expected

paragraphs.zh: 同伴不同意你觉得很清楚的安排，你开始把对方看成故意添乱。这个入口会先回到：我知道哪些实际情况，正在给对方加什么判断，眼前能怎样把分歧说清？你可以提出界限、要求补充信息或暂停讨论。认真回应不是忍受一切，也不保证对方马上改变。
paragraphs.en: A companion rejects an arrangement that seems clear to you, and you begin treating them as deliberately difficult. This entrance returns to what you actually know, the judgment you are adding and how to explain the present difference. You may set a boundary, request information or pause. A careful response does not require enduring everything or guarantee that another person changes.

title.zh: 把判断和下一步说具体
title.en: Making a judgment and next step specific

paragraphs.zh: 可以说：“我发现自己把不同意理解成不重视这件事，但还没有问清。现在我能先说明必要条件，再听你的看法。”这样的表达保留了自己的责任，也承认未知。不必声称毫无情绪，或要求别人也用同样方式回应；一句话说得平稳也不能证明处境已经安全或公平。
paragraphs.en: You might notice that you interpreted disagreement as indifference without checking, then explain the necessary conditions and invite the other account. That keeps responsibility for your next step while acknowledging uncertainty. You need not claim to feel nothing or require others to respond identically. An even delivery alone establishes neither safety nor fairness in the situation.

title.zh: 与其余八个阅读入口比较
title.en: Comparing the other eight reading entrances

paragraphs.zh: 爱比克泰德与马可·奥勒留共享斯多亚背景；本版前者聚焦判断与结果的区分，后者聚焦共同生活中的眼前回应，不是两套互斥人格。苏格拉底检视定义，亚里士多德关注具体实践，孔子关联学习反省与相处。老子检视多余强求，伊壁鸠鲁衡量追求及代价；尼采重估尺度，波伏瓦关注彼此自由。相同情境可以接续这些问题，并列不证明完整学说相同。
paragraphs.en: Epictetus and Marcus Aurelius share a Stoic background. This edition foregrounds judgment versus outcomes for the former and the present response in shared life for the latter, not two exclusive personalities. Socrates examines meanings, Aristotle particular practice and Confucius reflective learning in relationships. Laozi questions unnecessary forcing, Epicurus weighs pursuits and costs, Nietzsche reconsiders standards and Beauvoir attends to freedom with others. The questions may follow one another; a tie establishes no equivalence between complete doctrines.

title.zh: 认真回应不等于始终镇定
title.en: Careful responding does not require constant composure

paragraphs.zh: 你可能知道想怎样回应，却因为疲惫、压力或处境限制暂时做不到，也可能首先需要离开、休息或求助。这不由计数判成不够理性或自律。某些问题需要改变外部条件，不能只靠检视自己。测试没有评估危险、权力差距或应对资源，不替你要求忍耐。
paragraphs.en: You may know how you would like to respond but be unable to do so because of fatigue, pressure or circumstances, or first need distance, rest or assistance. Counts cannot label that insufficient reason or discipline. Some problems require external changes, not only self-examination. The set assesses no danger, power imbalance or coping resources and does not prescribe endurance.

title.zh: 区分一件小事里的事实与判断
title.en: Distinguishing facts and judgments in a small matter

paragraphs.zh: 愿意时，回顾一次低风险的小失望，分别写下已知情况、自己加上的判断和当时可选的一步。不必复现冲突，也不要求现在采取行动。你可以发现还需要别人的信息或实际支持。继续读第二卷时，把自我提醒放回文本语境，不把一句话变成要求自己永远镇定的命令。
paragraphs.en: If you wish, recall a low-stakes disappointment and distinguish what was known, the judgment you added and one option then available. No conflict needs reenacting and no action is required now. You may discover a need for information or practical support. Further reading can keep the reminders in context rather than converting a sentence into an order for permanent composure.

title.zh: 18题、8次曝光与全部并列
title.en: 18 questions, eight exposures and every tie

paragraphs.zh: 18题各选一项，合计18次；九类各出现8次，四个位置各2次。每选一次加1，未出现不算拒绝，8不是相似度百分比。全部最高并列完整显示；固定选同一位置会九类各2次。差一次不证明显著差异或思想身份，选择间也非九项独立特质。新版改变了对象与部分选项，不用新旧计数推断镇定或自律发生变化。
paragraphs.en: Eighteen single choices total 18 counts. Each of nine approaches appears eight times, twice in every position. Selections add one; absent options are not rejected and eight is not a similarity percentage. Every highest tie appears in full; choosing one position throughout gives two each. A one-choice difference establishes no significant difference or intellectual identity. These are not nine independent traits, and changed options prevent old and new counts from measuring changes in composure or discipline.

title.zh: 有限文本关联，不是心理训练或人物模拟
title.en: A limited textual association, not training or simulation

paragraphs.zh: 本结果不概括马可·奥勒留全部思想、真实人格或统治行为，也不因名字为任何历史行为背书。原典只提供所选问题的语境，不验证本站题目与计数；本文不复制现代译文。结果不评估理性、意志、道德、心理健康、宗教身份或职业，不能取代现实支持。可以保留提问方式，不接受人物标签。
paragraphs.en: This result summarises neither Marcus Aurelius’s whole thought nor his personality or rule, and the name endorses no historical action. The text contextualises a selected question without validating the items or counts; modern translations are not reproduced. Results assess no reason, willpower, morality, mental health, religion or career fit and cannot replace practical support. You can retain the question without adopting a personal label.

title.zh: 马可·奥勒留联想结果：判断与眼前回应
title.en: Marcus Aurelius Result: Judgment and the Present Response

description.zh: 阅读马可·奥勒留联想的《沉思录》语境、日常例子、八入口比较和计分说明。不把计数当镇定、自律或抗压能力。
description.en: Read the Marcus Aurelius association through Meditations Book II, examples, eight comparisons and scoring, without calmness, discipline or resilience ratings.

title.zh: 九个阅读联想怎样计数
title.en: How nine reading associations are counted

paragraphs.zh: 18题各选一项，对应阅读联想加1，次数合计18。每题提供九种思路中的四种；九类各出现8次，每个位置2次。未出现的五项不记为拒绝，分母8是曝光次数，不是相似度百分比、人群排名、人格强度或学说赞同率。所有最高计数保留全文，不用名单顺序硬派主副型；全选同一位置会九类各2，九份全部显示。相差一次只是一道选择，不证明显著差异或固定身份。近分可一起读，但不补造混合哲学家。计数是本题组选项的相对分布，一项被选时其他项没有被选，不是九项独立特质测量；时间、情境、熟悉程度与措辞都可能影响回答。新版改变了对象与部分选项，不能把新旧计数直接互认，或解释为思想、道德、人格及能力的进步或退步。
paragraphs.en: Choose one option for all eighteen questions; each adds one count and the total is eighteen. Each question offers four of nine approaches. Every approach appears eight times and twice in each position. Absent options are not counted as rejected. Eight is an exposure denominator rather than a similarity percentage, population rank, personality intensity or proportion of doctrine endorsed. Every highest count retains its full guide without list-order primary or secondary types. Choosing the same position throughout gives two each and displays all nine. A one-choice gap establishes no significant difference or fixed identity. Read close guides without inventing hybrid philosophers. Counts describe relative choices within this set rather than nine independent traits. Time, context, familiarity and wording can affect responses. This edition changes the figures and some options. Old and new counts are not directly interchangeable and cannot establish intellectual, moral, personality or ability progress or decline.

title.zh: 完整结果与原典语境
title.en: Full guides and primary-text context

paragraphs.zh: 九份说明各含原典语境、计数读法、当代具体例子、可用表达、其余八入口比较、反例、可选回顾、计分和范围。所有最高并列都完整呈现，其他正文始终公开可读。原典只支持所选思想背景，不验证题目映射、计数或个体解释；日常例子是本站原创，不冒充古代真实情境或哲学家原话。
paragraphs.en: Each of the nine guides includes textual context, count interpretation, a contemporary example, possible wording, eight comparisons, counterexamples, optional observation, scoring and scope. Every highest tie appears in full, with other guides remaining public. Texts support selected intellectual context rather than validating item mappings, counts or personal interpretation. Contemporary examples are independently authored rather than historical scenes or quotations attributed to philosophers.

title.zh: 不是人物性格或思想史考试
title.en: Not a historical personality or philosophy examination

paragraphs.zh: 九位是本版选取的哲学阅读入口，不是全体哲学家、完整思想史或心理学九型。苏格拉底依据柏拉图的记述；论语包括孔子及弟子言论；老子是文本传统名，不在本题裁定单一作者生平。原典仅为所选观念提供语境，不验证原创题目、映射、计数或个体解释。所有题目、选项、例子和报告为本站原创，不采用竞品题本标签正文或复制现代译文。计数不鉴定历史人物性格、智力、品德、宗教政治立场、文化身份、健康、关系或职业，不把某一种观念当现实行动命令。
paragraphs.en: These nine are selected reading entrances, not all philosophers, complete intellectual history or a psychological nine-type system. Socrates is approached through Plato; the Analects includes Confucius and disciples; Laozi names a textual tradition without this quiz deciding a single author’s biography. Primary texts contextualise selected ideas without validating original items, mappings, counts or personal interpretations. Questions, options, examples and reports are independently authored without competitor banks, labels or prose or reproduction of modern translations. Counts establish no historical personality, intelligence, morality, religion, politics, cultural identity, health, relationship or career, and no idea becomes a command for real-world action.

title.zh: 怎样使用原典链接
title.en: Using the primary-text links

paragraphs.zh: 苏格拉底入口用柏拉图《申辩篇》的记述；亚里士多德用《尼各马可伦理学》第二卷；孔子入口注意《论语》中不同说话者；老子入口读《道德经》第三十七、四十八章；伊壁鸠鲁用《致美诺伊克斯书》，爱比克泰德用《手册》开篇。链接是继续阅读的路径，不证明古人拥有本站九种人格。本站只原创转述所选观念及日常例子，不复制现代译文或竞品题本、模型标签、正文、代码和图片。
paragraphs.en: The Socrates entrance uses Plato’s Apology; Aristotle uses Nicomachean Ethics Book II. The Confucius entrance attends to different speakers in the Analects, while Laozi uses Daodejing chapters 37 and 48. Epicurus uses the Letter to Menoeceus and Epictetus the opening Enchiridion. Links provide further reading rather than evidence that historical people possessed nine website personalities. Selected ideas and examples are independently paraphrased without reproducing modern translations or competitor banks, labels, prose, code or art.

paragraphs.zh: 新增入口分别选取尼采《查拉图斯特拉如是说》第二部的自我超越问题、波伏瓦《模糊性的伦理学》中彼此自由与处境的讨论，以及马可·奥勒留《沉思录》第二卷的当下判断与回应。它们是有限原典阅读路径，不代表完整思想体系、真实人物性格或本站题目的测量效度。
paragraphs.en: The added entrances use self-overcoming in Part II of Nietzsche’s Thus Spoke Zarathustra, freedom with others and situated choice in Beauvoir’s The Ethics of Ambiguity, and present judgment and response in Book II of Marcus Aurelius’s Meditations. These are limited reading paths, not representations of complete systems, historical personalities or validation of this quiz.

title.zh: 完整免费、草稿与分享
title.en: Full free access, drafts and sharing

paragraphs.zh: 全部18题和九份九模块全文免费，无需注册、邮箱或其他测试解锁。答案在浏览器内计数，不上传、不进入网址或分析，不询问政治宗教身份与私人经历。草稿需主动开启，仅本标签页保留24小时，完成、重测或退出清除即删。可选分享只含公开阅读联想和链接，不含答案或次数。其他测评需要另行完整作答，不由哲学家名称换算MBTI、大五、健康、道德或职业。你可以直接先读正文，也可以在此结束。
paragraphs.en: All eighteen questions and nine full nine-section guides are free without signup, email or another test. Answers are counted in the browser without uploading or entering URLs or analytics; no political, religious identity or private history is requested. Opted-in drafts remain in this tab for 24 hours and clear on completion, retake or exit-and-clear. Optional sharing includes public reading associations and links without answers or counts. Other assessments require separate full answers rather than conversion from philosopher names into MBTI, Big Five, health, morality or career. You can read the guides first or stop here.

question.zh: 哲学家性格测试包括哪九位？

answer.zh: 本版自选苏格拉底、亚里士多德、孔子、老子、伊壁鸠鲁、爱比克泰德、尼采、波伏瓦和马可·奥勒留作有限原典阅读联想，不是全体哲学家或思想史排名。其他同名网站可能用不同人物、题目和方法，计数不能直接互认；本版新旧计数也不直接互认。
answer.en: This edition selects Socrates, Aristotle, Confucius, Laozi, Epicurus, Epictetus, Nietzsche, Simone de Beauvoir and Marcus Aurelius for limited reading associations, not all philosophers or a ranking of intellectual history. Websites sharing the name may use different figures, items and methods; their counts, and counts from our previous edition, are not directly interchangeable.

question.zh: 结果表示我像真实人物吗？
question.en: Does a result mean I resemble the real philosopher?

answer.zh: 九位是本版选取的哲学阅读入口，不是全体哲学家、完整思想史或心理学九型。苏格拉底依据柏拉图的记述；论语包括孔子及弟子言论；老子是文本传统名，不在本题裁定单一作者生平。原典仅为所选观念提供语境，不验证原创题目、映射、计数或个体解释。所有题目、选项、例子和报告为本站原创，不采用竞品题本标签正文或复制现代译文。计数不鉴定历史人物性格、智力、品德、宗教政治立场、文化身份、健康、关系或职业，不把某一种观念当现实行动命令。
answer.en: These nine are selected reading entrances, not all philosophers, complete intellectual history or a psychological nine-type system. Socrates is approached through Plato; the Analects includes Confucius and disciples; Laozi names a textual tradition without this quiz deciding a single author’s biography. Primary texts contextualise selected ideas without validating original items, mappings, counts or personal interpretations. Questions, options, examples and reports are independently authored without competitor banks, labels or prose or reproduction of modern translations. Counts establish no historical personality, intelligence, morality, religion, politics, cultural identity, health, relationship or career, and no idea becomes a command for real-world action.

question.en: How are counts and ties handled?

answer.zh: 18题各选一项，对应阅读联想加1，次数合计18。每题提供九种思路中的四种；九类各出现8次，每个位置2次。未出现的五项不记为拒绝，分母8是曝光次数，不是相似度百分比、人群排名、人格强度或学说赞同率。所有最高计数保留全文，不用名单顺序硬派主副型；全选同一位置会九类各2，九份全部显示。相差一次只是一道选择，不证明显著差异或固定身份。近分可一起读，但不补造混合哲学家。计数是本题组选项的相对分布，一项被选时其他项没有被选，不是九项独立特质测量；时间、情境、熟悉程度与措辞都可能影响回答。新版改变了对象与部分选项，不能把新旧计数直接互认，或解释为思想、道德、人格及能力的进步或退步。
answer.en: Choose one option for all eighteen questions; each adds one count and the total is eighteen. Each question offers four of nine approaches. Every approach appears eight times and twice in each position. Absent options are not counted as rejected. Eight is an exposure denominator rather than a similarity percentage, population rank, personality intensity or proportion of doctrine endorsed. Every highest count retains its full guide without list-order primary or secondary types. Choosing the same position throughout gives two each and displays all nine. A one-choice gap establishes no significant difference or fixed identity. Read close guides without inventing hybrid philosophers. Counts describe relative choices within this set rather than nine independent traits. Time, context, familiarity and wording can affect responses. This edition changes the figures and some options. Old and new counts are not directly interchangeable and cannot establish intellectual, moral, personality or ability progress or decline.

question.zh: 需要懂哲学或赞同全部学说吗？
question.en: Must I know philosophy or endorse a whole doctrine?

answer.zh: 不需要。题目没有哲学知识的正确答案，按目前更想先考虑的思路选择。一项选择不等于赞同某位的完整伦理、政治、宗教或人生观；也不测智力、道德、文化身份或专业能力。可以直接先读全部原典背景和全文。
answer.en: No. These choices have no correct philosophy-knowledge answers; choose the inquiry you currently prefer to consider first. One choice endorses no entire ethics, politics, religion or worldview and measures no intelligence, morality, cultural identity or professional skill. You can read every guide and its textual context first.

question.zh: 完整结果、重测和分享免费吗？
question.en: Are full results, retaking and sharing free?

answer.zh: 全部18题和九份九模块全文免费，无需注册、邮箱或其他测试解锁。答案在浏览器内计数，不上传、不进入网址或分析，不询问政治宗教身份与私人经历。草稿需主动开启，仅本标签页保留24小时，完成、重测或退出清除即删。可选分享只含公开阅读联想和链接，不含答案或次数。其他测评需要另行完整作答，不由哲学家名称换算MBTI、大五、健康、道德或职业。你可以直接先读正文，也可以在此结束。
answer.en: All eighteen questions and nine full nine-section guides are free without signup, email or another test. Answers are counted in the browser without uploading or entering URLs or analytics; no political, religious identity or private history is requested. Opted-in drafts remain in this tab for 24 hours and clear on completion, retake or exit-and-clear. Optional sharing includes public reading associations and links without answers or counts. Other assessments require separate full answers rather than conversion from philosopher names into MBTI, Big Five, health, morality or career. You can read the guides first or stop here.
